snip.t: *Which areas are affected – trunk, limbs, perineum?* — Dorsal column (vibration, proprioception) and spinothalamic tract (pain, temperature) are compressed.
A flat perineum with a short sacrum ("flat bottom") and meconium in the urine are indications for a protective colostomy.
Recognise it: the "turtle sign" (the head retracts against the perineum) and no restitution.

snip.t: Examine the baby (scalp, face, cranial nerves) and the mother (perineum, vagina), give antibiotics where indicated, and document indication, station, application and number of pulls.

snip.t: Protect the perineum, control the delivery of the head, check for the cord around the neck, then deliver the anterior shoulder (gentle downward traction) and the posterior shoulder.

qs.q: A patient undergoes an instrumental delivery using forceps. Examination of the perineum reveals a significant tear involving the anal sphincter. Which type of episiotomy, if performed, would have best reduced the risk of this extension?
qs.e: A mediolateral cut reduces the risk of extension into the anal sphincter compared to a midline cut. Midline cuts have a much higher rate of third and fourth-degree perineal tears.
qs.s: Operative Vaginal Delivery: Vacuum Extraction and Forceps: MCQs

qs.q: A 31-year-old gravida 2 para 1 at 39 weeks of gestation experiences shoulder dystocia following delivery of the fetal head, with retraction of the fetal chin against the perineum. What is the most appropriate initial maneuver?
o: Manual delivery of the posterior fetal arm vaginally
Direct downward pressure applied above the pubic bone
Internal rotation of the anterior fetal shoulder
Hyperflexion of the maternal thighs onto the abdomen
qs.e: Hyperflexion of the maternal thighs onto the abdomen (McRoberts position) flattens the sacral promontory and is the initial step in managing shoulder dystocia. Direct suprapubic pressure is applied after or concurrently with McRoberts positioning, not before.
qs.s: Shoulder Dystocia and Umbilical Cord Prolapse: Emergency Management: MCQs

qs.q: A newborn infant boy is noted to have an abnormality involving his perineum and scrotum. There is failure of midline fusion in the urogenital region. Chromosome analysis shows his karyotype is 46, XY. Which of the following is most likely responsible for his condition?
o: Failure of mesonephric ducts to reach the urogenital sinus
Failure of the urorectal septum to reach the perineum
qs.e: Testosterone is converted to dihydrotestosterone that induces labioscrotal swellings to fuse and become the scrotum.

qs.q: a 27-year-old man has complained of continuing 'jock itch' for the past year. On physical examination there are small whitish scaling patches on the skin of his perineum. A scraping from the lesion shows Trichophyton rubrum organisms. Which of the following lesions is he most likely to develop?
qs.e: The chronic rubbing and scratching from this dermatophyte infection can result in epidermal hyperplasia and chronic inflammation.
